final_message:
Fixed. A paid retry now moves the subscription back to `active`, and the reproduction test passes.

The cause was in `recover` in `billing/dunning.py`. When there were no other open invoices, the branch was just `pass`, so a past-due subscription never went back to active after its invoice was paid. I replaced `pass` with `transition(ctx, subscription, "active")`.

I ran your test as a temporary file, and it passes. I didn't add it to the suite. The existing 24 tests still pass and mypy is clean.

I also wrote `answer.json` in the repo root:

```json
{"file": "dunning.py", "function": "recover"}
```

steps.command: cd billing && ls && wc -l *.py && grep -n "past_due\|def advance\|retry" *.py | head -60; cat ../tests/conftest.py
cd billing && cat dunning.py payments.py; sed -n 85,135p engine.py

cd /tmp/bsvc-zqoxrtn9/billing-service && python3 - <<'E'
p='billing/dunning.py'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("    if not outstanding:\n        pass","    if not outstanding:\n        transition(ctx, subscription, \"active\")")
open(p,'w').write(s)
E
echo '{"file": "dunning.py", "function": "recover"}' > answer.json
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -5

cat > /tmp/test_r.py <<'E'
from tests.conftest import *
def test_r(world):
    cus = world.customer()
    world.gateway.fail_next.append("card_declined")
    sub = world.engine.subscribe(cus["id"], [(world.monthly["id"], 1)])
    assert sub["status"] == "past_due"
    world.advance_days(1)
    assert sub["status"] == "active"
    [inv] = world.engine.invoices_for(cus["id"])
    assert inv["status"] == "paid"
E
cp /tmp/test_r.py tests/test_tmp_r.py; .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_tmp_r.py 2>&1 | tail -3; rm tests/test_tmp_r.py; .venv/bin/python -m mypy billing | tail -1
